senses.definition: The name of a film, musical piece, painting, or other work of art.
examples: I know the singer's name, but not the title of the song.

senses.definition: The name of a writing such as a book, which identifies it and usually describes its subject, with a short phrase that often summarizes its topic.
(by extension) A published piece of media.
examples: The retailer carries thousands of titles.
Buyers of the new video game console can choose from three bundled titles.

senses.definition: (by extension) A section or division of a writing, as of an act of law or a book.
examples: Title II of the USA PATRIOT Act

senses.definition: An appellation given to a person or family to signify either veneration, official position, social rank, the possession of assets or properties, or a professional or academic qualification, such as Mister, Mr, Ms, Doctor, or Dr; for more examples, see :Category:en:Titles.

quotes.text: He read the letter aloud. Sophia listened with the studied air of one for whom, even in these days, a title possessed some surreptitious allurement.

senses.definition: (property law) Legal right to ownership of a property; a deed or other certificate proving this.
examples: a good title to an estate, or an imperfect title

translations.word: กรรมสิทธิ์

senses.definition: In canon law, that by which a beneficiary holds a benefice.
A church to which a priest was ordained, and where he was to reside.
(chiefly in the plural) A written title, credit, or caption shown with a film, video, or performance.
examples: The titles scrolled by too quickly to read.

senses.definition: (sports) The recognition given to the winner of a championship in sports.
(bookbinding) The panel for the name, between the bands of the back of a book.

senses.definition: (transitive) To assign a title to; to entitle.
(Internet slang) Used in the body of a post to indicate that the title has already said all that needs to be said.
